newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND HIT NEW LOW LOSING TO NEW ZEALAND A.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND HIT NEW LOW LOSING TO NEW ZEALAND A.

text.p: England's tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand hit a new nadir on Sunday when they were beaten by New Zealand A by 90 runs on the last morning of their four-day match.
It was the first time a touring side had been beaten by a New Zealand non-test team in a first class match since 1982/83 when Canterbury beat Sri Lanka.
England's hopes in the match were always slim after they were bowled out in their first innings for 107.
They began the day at 166 for six, needing 363 for victory.
England's hopes of an unlikely win rose briefly as Jack Russell and Robert Croft batted through the first 75 minutes.
Then Croft was smartly caught at short leg for 49 and the remaining wickets fell in quick succession.
Andrew Caddick holed out to backward point for 12, Chris Silverwood was run out after being sent back the length of the pitch for 10 and Phil Tufnell carelessly slogged an easy catch to mid off.
Russell was left unbeaten on 61 off 137 balls.
Left armer Geoff Allott, recalled for this week's second test in Wellington, took four for 76 while the other wickets were shared around.
It was England's second first-class loss on their winter tour to non-test opposition.
They were beaten by Mashonaland early in the Zimbabwe leg of their trip.
The second test starts at the Basin Reserve on Thursday.
